description: Per-category production profiles used to turn each catalog capability into a concrete contract: default phase, engine/language family, expected artifacts, acceptance checks, risk register entries, verification intents, and approval-sensitive actions. Editable by design; command hints are advisory and must be confirmed against the exact engine/editor version in use.

phase-1.label: Reliable Foundation
phase-1.goal: Version intelligence, project creation, source control, core gameplay, input, UI, saves, tests, builds, and documentation.
phase-1.exit_criteria: A clean machine can build and start the project from the locked dependency set and pass the documented smoke checks.

phase-2.label: Complete Playable Production
phase-2.goal: Levels, graphics, animation, audio, AI, physics, progression, deployment, performance, and platform adaptation.
phase-2.exit_criteria: The full gameplay loop is playable end to end inside the performance budget on declared target hardware.

phase-3.label: Advanced Systems
phase-3.goal: Multiplayer, backend, procedural generation, XR, custom engines, compilers, modding, live services, and specialized platforms.
phase-3.exit_criteria: Advanced systems are observable, bounded, and covered by automated or scripted verification.

phase-4.label: Scale and Trust
phase-4.goal: Security, privacy, accessibility, compliance, certification, CI/CD, telemetry, regression testing, archival, and disaster recovery.
phase-4.exit_criteria: Release evidence exists for security, privacy, accessibility, reproducibility, and recovery, and human approvals are recorded.

phase-5.label: Autonomous Creation
phase-5.goal: Multimodal briefs, engine routing, prototype generation, repository repair, adaptive tests, approvals, and end-to-end orchestration.
phase-5.exit_criteria: Every automated change is traceable to a request, every risky action carries an approval record, and the artifact set is reproducible.

artifacts.purpose: Makes mod loading deterministic.

checks.statement: User content cannot read arbitrary files, open sockets, or execute native code through the API
Invalid or conflicting content is rejected with a specific message and does not break the game
Load order resolution is deterministic for the same content set

risks.risk: Mod API becomes an arbitrary code execution path
risks.mitigation: Expose a curated API, deny filesystem and network by default, and test escape attempts

risks.risk: API changes break the creator ecosystem
risks.mitigation: Version the API, deprecate with a window, and keep compatibility shims

verification.intent: Run the sandbox escape test suite
Load a deliberately broken mod and record the error path

artifacts.title: Provenance and lawfulness note for every recovered artifact
artifacts.purpose: Keeps the work lawful and auditable.

artifacts.title: Format and behavior mapping table
artifacts.purpose: Maps original behavior to the port.

artifacts.title: Parity test results against the original
artifacts.purpose: Proves fidelity claims.

checks.statement: Original artifacts are preserved unmodified with recorded hashes before any conversion
Converted data and behavior pass declared parity checks against the original
Legal basis (ownership, license, permission) is documented before analysis or redistribution
checks.evidence: provenance note reviewed by a human

risks.risk: Working on assets without rights creates legal exposure
risks.mitigation: Require documented legal clearance before touching binaries or shipping derived assets

risks.risk: Original behavior is lost when artifacts are overwritten
risks.mitigation: Copy and hash originals first, work only on copies

verification.intent: Hash and archive the originals before conversion
Run parity checks and record differences per mapped behavior

artifacts.title: Request-to-task traceability map
artifacts.purpose: Proves every change answers a request item.

artifacts.title: Engine and language routing record with rationale
artifacts.purpose: Makes routing auditable and revisable.

artifacts.title: Approval ledger for risky actions
artifacts.purpose: Shows who approved what before it happened.

checks.statement: Every generated change traces to a request item and a capability id
checks.evidence: traceability map plus commit or diff references

checks.statement: Risky actions (publish, delete, credentials, payments, signing) carry a recorded approval before execution
checks.evidence: approval ledger entries with approver and timestamp

checks.statement: The orchestration run is reproducible from the recorded inputs and seeds
checks.evidence: two-run comparison of plan ids and artifact hashes

risks.risk: An agent performs an unattended destructive or publishing action
risks.mitigation: Gate risky actions behind an explicit approval ledger entry and default to dry runs

risks.risk: Generated work drifts from the request without anyone noticing
risks.mitigation: Require a traceability map entry per change and review it at each gate

verification.intent: Diff the traceability map against the actual changed files
Re-run the plan with identical inputs and compare plan ids

universal_checks.statement: The deliverable is editable source plus explicit build or run instructions, not a compiled black box
universal_checks.evidence: source files present plus a run command and its expected output

universal_checks.statement: At least one automated or scripted check exists for this capability and it can actually fail
universal_checks.evidence: test output showing a pass run and a deliberately induced failure

universal_checks.statement: Exact engine, editor, language, SDK, and dependency versions are recorded with the artifact
universal_checks.evidence: version matrix or lock file stored beside the deliverable

universal_checks.statement: The handoff names the next owner, the exact commands to run, and the known limitations
universal_checks.evidence: handoff section with owner, commands, and limitation list
